title: Partner notification subscription
description: A partner registration: one commuter's recurring journey plus a callback destination. It is /varsel's own registration shape (origin place, destination place, weekdays, a daily boarding window in Europe/Oslo) so that a partner subscription and a browser registration with the same definition see the same trains and cost one match and one wording between them. Authored here and rendered as OpenAPI by the partner API rather than redefined there. The recipient behind a subscription is a commuter on a monthly pass, not a ticket-holder for one departure, which is why the grain is a recurring window and why the daily cap is per subscription.

subscription_id.description: Caller-supplied, which is what makes a create safely retryable: the same id with the same definition returns the stored record and writes nothing, while the same id with a different definition is refused rather than silently overwriting a live subscription.

partner_id.description: Read-only. Taken from the authenticated credential, never from the request body: a partner may manage only its own subscriptions, and accepting this field from the caller would make that a request-shaped choice.

destination_id.description: Which provisioned callback destination this subscription's events are delivered to. One per environment per partner in the pilot. Signing secrets are per destination, so this is also what decides which secret an attempt is signed under.

from_stop.description: Origin, a National Stop Register stop place. Canonicalized on read: refs the registry has collapsed onto one physical place must land on one journey key, or the same physical trip earns two matches, two wordings and two notifications.

to_stop.description: Destination, a National Stop Register stop place. Must differ from from_stop.

begin.description: Start of the daily boarding window, HH:MM in Europe/Oslo.

end.description: End of the daily boarding window, HH:MM in Europe/Oslo. Must be strictly after begin: overnight windows are rejected here exactly as they are in /varsel, so a partner cannot register a window /varsel would not.

days.description: Weekdays the window applies on, 0 = Monday.

partner_ref.description: The partner's own opaque reference, echoed in every event so normal receipt needs no second request to us. Opaque to us: never parsed, never logged, never used as a key.

test.description: Marks the subscription as test-only. IMMUTABLE -- changing it requires delete and re-create -- because it rides inside the signed event body and the receiver refuses a test event before native dispatch unless the adapter has opted into an isolated test recipient map. A subscription that could be flipped live would turn every previously-signed test event into a real notification.

version.description: Read-only, monotonic per subscription, bumped by every amendment and by the tombstone. An amendment may be conditioned on it, and an event carries the version it was authorised by so a delete or amendment racing an emission rejects the obsolete one.

status.description: Read-only. `deleted` is a tombstone written in a single transaction that stops routing; the events, deliveries and subjects behind it are then removed by a retryable cleanup task with an auditable completion state, and the tombstone's own route is redacted the moment that completes.

servable.description: Whether any planned direct trip runs between the two places. `null` means the answer could not be established -- an outage, a timeout -- and must never render as an all-clear. A subscription no direct trip can serve carries the caveat and is NEVER refused: weekend-only and seasonal routes are why a refusal would be wrong.

servable_checked_at.description: How fresh the servability answer is. Missing or stale data never reads as an all-clear.

expires_at.description: Read-only. The earlier of a 180-day maximum lifetime from creation and a 60-day inactivity horizon from the last partner interaction. Both are enforced on READ as well as by the store's TTL, because TTL deletion runs up to ~24 hours late and a subscription that kept alerting for a day past its published expiry would be a broken promise rather than a slow cleanup.

alerts.description: Current alert state: what stands right now about this subscription, read from the notification service's own committed alert subjects rather than re-evaluated. Present on both GET routes; `null` on the response to a create or replace, which does not read it -- so `null` means "not included in this response" and never "no standing alerts". The latter is `n_active: 0` with `truncated: false`.

n_active.description: Standing alerts -- predicted or confirmed. A withdrawn alert is not one and is not counted.

n_confirmed.description: How many of those are confirmed cancellations rather than forecasts.

truncated.description: True when the read was bounded by its ceiling or could not be completed. The counts are then LOWER BOUNDS: `n_active: 0` beside this means "we could not establish it", never "all clear". On a list page it is set on every row whenever that page's single query was bounded, because a subscription crowded out of the page would otherwise read exactly like a calm one -- ask about it individually and the read is scoped to it alone.

subjects.description: The worst few standing alerts, worst first: a confirmed cancellation ahead of a forecast, then most recently changed, ties broken on `alert_id` so the order cannot flip between two requests about unchanged data. Deliberately capped at the number of notifications one subscription can receive in an Oslo day -- a longer list would enumerate what that cap has already suppressed -- and the counts above carry the rest, so nothing is hidden, only unenumerated.

phase.description: A withdrawn alert does not stand and is never listed.

delivered_revision.description: The highest revision about this train that was delivered to you, or null if none has been -- an alert we hold and you do not.
